Uncertain Archive · 45 bags · supervised vs. unsupervised

Your piles, its piles

Forty-five bags from my archive, loose on the table. Move them around and make piles however you see them. Open a photo to look closer or give it one of my labels, if you want. Then let the machine arrange the same photos with no labels at all, only what it can measure in the pixels.

Drag photos into piles · tap a photo to open it · while you hold one, the machine shows what it thinks belongs with it
Two ways of sorting
  • You know what a bag is. You can sort by material, color, shape, where you saw it, or a feeling. Your labels are limited to my six classes: Woven, Leather, Cotton, Suede, Unsure, Seen/Saved.
  • The machine never learns the word "bag." It reads each whole photo as color, brightness, edges and layout, then groups what looks alike (unsupervised k-means clustering).
  • After the reveal, each photo carries the name of the pile you put it in, so you can watch where your piles go.
  • Tap a photo after the reveal to compare three readings: yours, the clustering, and Teachable Machine trained on my labels.
